audit_result.proof_trace: The proof fails: the code enforces `repay_amount <= debt_balance * close_factor` (L1008-1011) — a static global parameter — instead of the dynamic formula R_max = (WD - WC) / (w_d - LT_liq × (1+incentive)) required to bring weighted_debts' == weighted_collateral' (risk == 1.0). For a barely-unhealthy position (e.g., WD=1021, WC=1020, LTV_liq=0.85, incentive=0.05), R_max ≈ 9.3 but close_factor×D ≈ 510, allowing ~55× over-liquidation; the spec INV-001 and the module comment in liquidate.move explicitly require the cap to equal R_max.
audit_result.attack_scenario: A whitelisted LiquidationBot calls `liquidate()` on an obligation that is barely unhealthy (weighted_debts just above weighted_collateral by ε). The bot supplies `available_repay_coin = close_factor × debt_balance`, which passes the close_factor assertion but is orders of magnitude larger than R_max for that position; the borrower loses up to 50% of their total debt in collateral (at the liquidation incentive premium) when less than 1% repayment was sufficient to restore health.

PROP-current-fina-inv-014.text: After soft liquidation, obligation risk level (debt_value / collateral_value) must equal exactly 1.0.
